findings.label: N
findings.finding: falsifier.tier_1.machine_checkable_steps overstates machine checkability: of the four items, only 'constraint residuals below tolerance' has a general decision procedure. 'g-prime continuous and nondegenerate on a neighbourhood of the boundary (sampled)' is numerical evidence, not a check; 'iota is an isometry onto an open proper subset' and 'the added points lie in the future of iota(M)' are proof obligations. non_machine_checkable_step names only non-meagerness and therefore understates the set.
findings.recommendation: Split the list into (i) machine-checkable residuals, (ii) numerically checkable on an explicit finite representation, (iii) proof obligations. Same class of defect as the F2a sibling finding; one correlated finding across the two artifacts.
findings.independence: I re-derived this from the text before reading reviews/F2b-review-18.json; it confirms worker-18 F-B3 independently and DISAGREES with F2b-review-16-r3, which recorded the topic as well handled. findings.label: N
findings.finding: Domain/binder type mismatch in D0: the binder is the pair '(s,delta)' but D0 is 'Sobolev variant s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1), or the smooth-with-decay default', whose second member is not a pair. The smooth branch's decay rates still reference s ('1 <= k <= s', '0 <= k <= s-1', lines 140-141) although s is only defined for the Sobolev branch; line 149 repeats the disjunction.
findings.recommendation: Encode D0 as a tagged set of regularity settings (or state the smooth member explicitly with 'for all k'), so the binder type covers every member. This matches the F0 rev4 wording 'for every admissible (s,delta)' at the statement level but not at the type level.
